paper.citation: Dimitriadis, T., Dümbgen, L., Henzi, A., Puke, M. and Ziegel, J. (2023). Honest calibration assessment for binary outcome predictions. Biometrika, 110(3), 663-680. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asac068.
paper.venue: Biometrika (formal publication, 2023); arXiv preprint v2 is the checked DGP version
paper.source_locator: DGP source actually checked in arXiv:2203.04065v2 (2022-11-02), PDF p.8, Section 5, item 5 (Wave): p_s(x)=0.5-(2s-1)(x-0.5)+8s(x-0.5)^3, s in {0,0.1,...,1}; X~U[0,1] and Y~Bernoulli{p_s(X)} are specified on the same page. Supplementary Material PDF pp.17-20 covers rounding, application details and proofs and does not state a changed wave DGP. The paper gives replication URL https://github.com/marius-cp/replication_DDHPZ22 but no fixed code commit. Formal Biometrika DGP differences were not checked [*].

mechanism.name: Cubic wave binary regression functions from Dimitriadis et al. (2023)

generation_equations.label: Special values
generation_equations.expression: p_s(0)=0; p_s(0.5)=0.5 for all s; p_s(1)=1; s=0 reduces to p(x)=x (excluded as duplicate)

sampling.dependence: iid across observations; no cluster, panel, network, or within-unit dependence

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed individual observations (X_i,Y_i).
X has the source distribution Uniform[0,1] and the fixed query x*=0.5 lies in its support interior.
Given X=x, Y is Bernoulli with success probability p_s(x)=0.5-(2s-1)(x-0.5)+8s(x-0.5)^3.

Monotonicity of p_s holds only for s<=0.5 (p_s'(x)=-(2s-1)+24s(x-0.5)^2 >= 0 on [0,1] iff s<=0.5). Scenarios s=0.6,...,1.0 are non-monotone stress scenarios: the source's simultaneous-band coverage theorem under monotonicity does NOT apply to them, and no monotone-band coverage is claimed there.
For all declared s, p_s(0)=0, p_s(0.5)=0.5, p_s(1)=1 and p_s([0,1]) is within [0,1] up to floating-point rounding (clamped in generation).
The scalar truth is evaluated under the known DGP; no causal exchangeability, treatment, mediator, or interference assumption is relevant.

properties.notes: The only covariate is X, so total and effective dimensions are both one. There are no interaction terms. The regression function is a cubic polynomial in (x-0.5): 8s(x-0.5)^3-(2s-1)(x-0.5)+0.5, nonlinear for s>0 (and linear at s=0, which is excluded as a degenerate duplicate). The binary outcome link is Bernoulli with this conditional probability. Monotonicity of p_s holds only for s<=0.5; for s>0.5 the curve has a local maximum and minimum inside (0,1), so those scenarios are registered as assumption-violation stress tests, not as valid monotone-band cases.

estimand.name: m_s(x*) = E[Y | X=x*] = p_s(x*)
estimand.definition: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0.1,0.2,...,1.0}; the wave function is the cubic polynomial p_s(x)=0.5-(2s-1)(x-0.5)+8s(x-0.5)^3 (equivalently 8s*x^3-12s*x^2+(4s+1)*x). The target is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.

truth.expression: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0.1,0.2,...,1.0}; the wave function is the cubic polynomial p_s(x)=0.5-(2s-1)(x-0.5)+8s(x-0.5)^3 (equivalently 8s*x^3-12s*x^2+(4s+1)*x). The target is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.
truth.derivation: Analytic: at x*=0.5 both (x-0.5) and (x-0.5)^3 vanish, so p_s(0.5)=0.5 for every s. Independently audited via the expanded polynomial form 8s*x^3-12s*x^2+(4s+1)*x evaluated at x=0.5, and via symbolic factoring. Default s=0.5 gives exactly 0.5.

adaptations: Register s=0.1,0.2,...,1.0 as named scenarios; exclude s=0 because it degenerates to p(x)=x, which is duplicated across the monomial/s-shape/kink/step templates at their s=0 endpoints.
Expose the scalar NRI target p_s(0.5)=E[Y|X=0.5] required by the collection interface. The source studies simultaneous confidence bands under monotonicity, not this scalar truth hook.

Mark scenarios s=0.6,...,1.0 as assumption-violation stress scenarios: p_s is non-monotone there, so the source's monotonicity-based coverage theorem does not apply. These are retained for stress testing, not for claiming valid monotone-band coverage.
Run the collection smoke check instead of the source's 1000-replication coverage experiment; no confidence band, bootstrap, or coverage result is claimed.
